title: Odd stochastic density functional theory
authors: Yael Avni, Michel Fruchart, David Martin, Tali Khain, Vincenzo Vitelli
abstract: Stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) provides a powerful framework for studying the dynamics of many-body systems both in and out of equilibrium. In its standard form, it can be viewed as a density-based formulation of coupled Langevin equations with white noise. Here, we extend SDFT to a class of systems, ranging from magnetized electrolytes to chiral active matter, that possess a chiral overdamped limit in which a relaxation timescale and an oscillation period are simultaneously taken to zero. We derive this formulation, which we dub ``odd SDFT", by taking the overdamped limit of a fluctuating hydrodynamic description of underdamped particles subject to a Lorentz force. We establish the validity and utility of the resulting framework by calculating the collective mobility tensor of interacting particles using both direct linear response and a Green-Kubo relation. We then apply the theory to the Hall conductivity of electrolytes in magnetic fields. Going beyond mean-field theory and using two distinct Green-Kubo relations, we derive the full conductivity tensor, extending the relaxation part of the Debye-Hückel-Onsager theory to the case of finite magnetic fields.
summary: This paper introduces 'odd Stochastic Density Functional Theory' (odd SDFT) to model complex, chiral many-body systems like magnetized electrolytes. It extends standard SDFT by deriving a new formulation applicable when relaxation and oscillation periods vanish simultaneously. The theory successfully calculates the full, asymmetric conductivity tensor, providing a systematic tool for studying odd transport phenomena beyond mean-field approximations.
main_problem: The paper extends Stochastic Density Functional Theory (SDFT) to model systems exhibiting chirality, specifically addressing the 'chiral overdamped limit' where both relaxation time and oscillation period vanish.
main_result: The authors derive 'odd SDFT,' a framework that systematically computes odd (or Hall) response functions and transport coefficients, extending classical theories like Debye-Hückel-Onsager to finite magnetic fields.
method: The theory is derived by taking the overdamped limit of a fluctuating hydrodynamic description of underdamped particles subject to a Lorentz force, utilizing linear response theory and Green-Kubo relations.
model_or_system: The theory applies to general chiral systems, including magnetized electrolytes and chiral active matter. The underlying dynamics are modeled via fluctuating Langevin equations incorporating a Lorentz force and chiral noise.
key_observables: Hall conductivity tensor ($\mathbf{K}$), collective mobility tensor ($\mathbf{L}$), and the full conductivity tensor components ($\kappa_0, \kappa_H, \kappa_\parallel$).
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength ($B$), correlation time ($	au$), and the characteristic frequency ($\omega$) defining the chiral noise regime.
main_assumptions: The derivation involves adiabatically eliminating the momentum field in the low-mass limit, and the standard SDFT formulation assumes white noise, which is insufficient for magnetized electrolytes.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the collective linear response to a spatiotemporal force, showing the development of a transverse current. Figure 3 shows the calculated Hall conductance components as a function of a magnetic field parameter.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the odd SDFT framework by deriving it from the overdamped limit of fluctuating hydrodynamics. It then establishes its utility by calculating the collective mobility tensor using Green-Kubo relations and applies it to derive the full conductivity tensor for electrolytes in magnetic fields, comparing results across multiple theoretical approaches.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the development of a generalized, non-equilibrium response theory (odd SDFT) that handles non-Hermitian or chiral couplings is highly relevant to open quantum systems and non-Markovian dynamics in quantum optics.
